alignments.note: Ordinary connective.
Inflected verb takes its supplied subject and auxiliary under rules 7 and 9; head on the lexical verb.
Article surfaces as English 'the' under rule 19; the genitive is governed by the verb and the ASV writes no case preposition, so nothing else rides here.
Noun stands alone, its determiner on the article under rule 21.
Relative pronoun to its relativizer; no supplied nominal competes, so rule 77 keeps the head on 'which'.
Finite verb alone; the English 'with' answers to the dative pronoun's case, not to the verb, under rules 21 and 36, even though 'reason with' reads as phrasal.
Dative pronoun with its case preposition riding along under rule 21; the ASV supplies no determiner, so 'with' stays on the pronoun.
Comparative adverb takes its own 'as'; no correlative 'so' stands, so rules 82 and 100 are not in question.
Anarthrous dative noun with its case preposition; no article stands to anchor a determiner, so 'with' rides with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause.
Genitive pronoun carries the English possessive; the vocative is anarthrous, so no article is in question under rule 20.
Anarthrous vocative noun stands bare, the possessive belonging to the genitive pronoun.
Ordinary negative 'not'; no negative indefinite follows, so rules 41 and 59 do not apply.

Discontinuous under rule 15, the negative standing between. Head on 'lightly' under rules 17 and 91: the corpus has no unit for this hapax lemma, but the adverb is what glosses the oligo- root while 'regard' is the generic verb supplying the frame, as 'think it strange' heads on 'strange'. Heading on 'regard' as the finite verb remains defensible and is the competing reading.
Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied 'the' is an ordinary rule 7/51 helper on the noun it determines.
Anarthrous genitive: the supplied determiner and the case preposition both ride with the noun, headed on the noun under rule 17.
Negative conjunction to 'Nor'.
Imperative to its English verb.
Participle expanded into a finite subordinate clause: the supplied subordinator, subject and copula are rule 7 helpers on the participle, which is the token carrying the subordination under rule 86.
Preposition to the English preposition governing its pronoun under rule 36.
Governed pronoun stands on its own English word.

review_notes: All 20 source and 31 target ids partitioned exactly once.
s013 head is the one genuinely contested choice: 'lightly' over 'regard', argued from rule 91's operational test with no corpus attestation for the lemma.
s003 takes a bare 'the' with no 'of', the genitive being verb-governed; s015 by contrast is anarthrous and carries its own supplied 'the' and 'of' under rule 21's determinerless clause.
